verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              धर्मराजस्य तद्वाक्यं निशम्य शिनिपुङ्गवः।  स पार्थाद्भयमाशंसन् परित्यागान्महीपतेः॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Hearing those words of the very virtuous king Yudhishthira, that foremost of the Sinis, became afraid of the reproach he would incur at Arjuna's hands, it he would leave the king.

verses.sanskrit: अपवादं ह्यात्मनश्च लोकात् पश्यन् विशेषतः।  ते मां भीतमिति ब्रूयुरायान्तं फाल्गुनं प्रति ॥२॥
verses.english: But seeing certainly of an imputation of cowardice by the people (if he were to disobey the words of Yudhishthira), he thus thought within himself. “Let not men say that I am afraid of proceeding to the rescue of Arjuna.

verses.sanskrit: निश्चित्य बहुधैवं स सात्यकेर्युद्धदुर्मदः।  धर्मराजमिदं वाक्यमब्रवीत् पुरुषर्षभः ॥३॥
verses.english: Thus thinking over the matter in various ways, that foremost of men, the invincible Satyaki, spoke these words to the very virtuous king Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: कृतां चेन्मन्यसे रक्षां स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु विशांपते।  अनुयास्यामि बीभत्सुं करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥४॥
न हि मे पाण्डवात् कश्चित्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते।  यो मे प्रियतरो राजन् सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि ते॥५॥
verses.english: There is nothing dearer to my soul in the three worlds, then that son of Pandu (Arjuna). This I tell you in all earnestness.

verses.sanskrit: तस्याहं पदवीं यास्ये सन्देशात्तव मानद।  त्वत्कृते न च मे किंचिदकर्तव्यं कथञ्चन ॥६॥
verses.english: O bestower of honor, with your permission, I will follow his track. There is nothing that I shall not do for your sake.

verses.sanskrit: यथा हि मे गुरोर्वाक्यं विशिष्टं द्विपदां वर।  तथा तवापि वचनं विशिष्टतरमेव मे ॥७॥
verses.english: 0 best of men, the commands of my preceptor are ever worthy of my attention. But your words are all the more so.

verses.sanskrit: प्रिये हि तव वर्तेते भ्रातरौ कृष्णपाण्डवौ।  तयोः प्रिये स्थितं चैव विद्धि मां राजपुंगव ॥८॥
तवाज्ञां शिरसा गृह्य पाण्डवार्थमहं प्रभो। भित्त्वेदं दुर्भिदं सैन्यं प्रयास्ये नरपुंगव ॥९॥
verses.english: Holding your behest on my head, I will, O lord, proceed piercing this impenetrable army, for rendering help, O best of men, to that son of Pandu.

verses.sanskrit: द्रोणानीकं विशाम्येष क्रुद्धो झष इवार्णवम्। तत्र यास्यामि यत्रासौ राजन् राजा जयद्रथः॥१०॥
verses.english: Here shall, I plunge into the divisions of Drona, excited as I am with rage. I shall then dart through it like a fish through the ocean, O king, to the spot where king Jayadratha.

verses.sanskrit: यत्र सेनां समाश्रित्य भीतस्तिष्ठति पाण्डवात्। गुप्तो रथवरश्रेष्ठैर्द्रोणिकर्णकृपादिभिः॥११॥
verses.english: Stays, protected by his troops and trembling in fear of the son of Pandu and depending upon those feremost of car-warriors viz., Drona's son, Karna, Kripa and others.

verses.sanskrit: इतस्त्रियोजनं मन्ये तमध्वानं विशांपते। यत्र तिष्ठति पार्थोऽसौ जयद्रथवधोद्यतः ॥१२॥
वियोजनगतस्यापि तस्य यास्याम्यहं पदम्। आसैन्धववधाद्राजन् सुदृढेनान्तरात्मना ॥१३॥
verses.english: But through Partha is three Yojanas away from this place, yet I shall pursue his track with a firm heart and support him till the slaughter of Jayadratha in accomplished.

verses.sanskrit: अनादिष्टस्तु गुरुणा को नु युध्येत मानवः। आदिष्टस्तु यथा राजन् को न युध्येत मादृशः॥१४॥
verses.english: Unless commanded by his preceptors, what man goes to battle with his enemies? When again commanded, O king, like myself, by his preceptors, what man is there that would not fight?

verses.sanskrit: अभिजानामि तं देशं यत्र यास्याम्यहं प्रभो। हलशक्तिगदाप्रासचर्मखड्गर्ष्टितोमरम् ॥१५॥
verses.english: I know the spot, O king, whither I have to go. Teeming as it does with plough-shares, lances, maces darts, bludgeons.

verses.sanskrit: इष्वस्त्रवरसंबाधं क्षोभयिष्ये बलार्णवम्। यदेतत्कुञ्जरानीकं साहस्रमनुपश्यसि ॥१६॥
verses.english: Arrows and other weapons, I shall still agitate this ocean-like host. This elephant division, numbering a thousand elephants strong, that you see.

verses.sanskrit: कुलमाञ्जनकं नाम यत्रैते वीर्यशालिनः। आस्थिता बहुभिर्म्लेच्छैर्युद्धशौण्डेः प्रहारिभिः॥१७॥
verses.english: All belonging to the breed known as Arjuna and all possessed of great prowess and ridden by numerous Mlechchas delighting in battle and skilled in smiting down.

verses.sanskrit: नागा मेघनिभा राजन् क्षरन्त इव तोयदाः। नैते जातु निवर्तेरन् प्रेषिता हस्तिसादिभिः ॥१८॥
verses.english: These elephants shedding the temporal juice like clouds pouring rain, they never turn back when goaded on by those on their backs.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यत्र हि वधादेषां नास्ति राजन् पराजयः। अथ यान् रथिनो राजन् सहस्रमनुपश्यसि ॥१९॥
verses.english: They cannot be defeated unless they are slaughtered, Oking. Then again you carwarriors thousands strong in number, whom you can see.

verses.sanskrit: एते रुक्मरथा नाम राजपुत्रा महारथाः। रथेष्वस्त्रेषु निपुणा नागेषु च विशांपते॥२०॥
verses.english: Are of royal extraction and are all recongnised as Maharathas. All of them are of golden chariots. They accomplished in the use of weapons, in fighting upon cars and on the backs of elephants, O king!

verses.sanskrit: धनुर्वेदे गताः पारं मुष्टियुद्धे च कोविदाः। गदायुद्धविशेषज्ञा नियुद्धकुशलास्तथा ॥२१॥
verses.english: Masters in the art of bowmanship, they are well-skilled in fighting with their fist also. They are skilled in fighting with maces and also in close quarters.

verses.sanskrit: खड्गप्रहरणे युक्ताः संपाते चासिचर्मणोः। शूराश्च कृतविद्याश्च स्पर्धन्ते च परस्परम् ॥२२॥
verses.english: They are equally active in fighting with the sword and falling upon the foe with sword and buckler. They are courageous, learned and inspired with a desire for outvieing one another. Owners are

verses.sanskrit: नित्यं हि समरे राजन् ‌विजिगीषन्ति मानवान्। कर्णेन विहिता राजन् दुःशासनमनुव्रताः ॥२३॥
verses.english: O king, they every day conquer countless warriors. They are under Karna's commanded and devotedly follow Dushasana.

verses.sanskrit: एतांस्तु वासुदेवोऽपि रथोदारान् प्रशंसति। सततं प्रियकामाश्च कर्णस्यैते वशे स्थिताः॥२४॥
verses.english: Even Vasudeva's son praises these men as mighty car-warriors. Always solicitous of doing good to the Kurus, they are obedient to Karna.

verses.sanskrit: तस्यैव वचनाद्राजन् निवृत्ताः श्वेतवाहनात्। ते न क्लान्ता न च श्रान्ता दृढावरणकार्मुकाः॥२५॥
verses.english: Returning, at Karna's command, from their pursuit of Arjuna of white steeds and so unfatigued and in-exhausted, those brave warriors, accoutered in impenetrable mail and armed with tough bows.

verses.sanskrit: मदर्थेऽधिष्ठिता नूनं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य शासनात्। एतान् प्रमथ्य संग्रामे प्रियार्थं तव कौरव ॥२६॥
verses.english: Are made to wait for me at Duryodhana's command. For your good, O foremost descendant of the Kuru race, crushing these warriors in battle.

verses.sanskrit: प्रयास्यामि ततः पश्चात् पदवीं सव्यसाचिनः।  यांस्त्वेतानपरान्राजन्नागान्सप्त शतानिमान्॥२७॥
verses.english: I will follow from behind the track laid open by Savyasachin. Those other elephants, O monarch, full seven hundred in number.

verses.sanskrit: प्रेक्षसे वर्मसंछन्नान् किरातैः समधिष्ठितान्।  किरातराजो यान् प्रादाद्द्विरदान् सव्यसाचिनः ॥२८॥
verses.english: That you can see, all covered with armours, ridden by Kiratas and adorned with ornaments, were formerly presented by the king of the Kiratas, together with many servants, to Savyasachin; O King these were at first engaged in doing your good.

verses.sanskrit: स्वलंकृतांस्तदा प्रेष्यानिच्छन् जीवितमात्मनः।  आसन्नेते पुरा राजंस्तव कर्मकरा दृढम् ॥२९॥
त्वामेवाद्य युयुत्सन्ते पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम्।  एषामेते महामात्राः किराता युद्धदुर्मदाः ॥३०॥
verses.english: Behold the changes brought about by time, in as mush as, they are now ranged to fight against you. The Kiratas indomitable, in battle are their guides. Skillful in guiding elephants and all sprung from fire, they were all unitedly defeated in battle by Savyasachin.

verses.sanskrit: हस्तिशिक्षाविद‌श्चैव सर्वे चैवाग्नियोनयः।  एते विनिर्जिताः संख्ये संग्रामे सव्यसाचिना॥३१॥
मदर्थमद्य संयत्ता दुर्योधनवशानुगाः।  एतान् हत्वा शरै राजन् किरातान् युद्धदुर्मदान् ॥३२॥
verses.english: Obedient to the commands of Duryodhana, they are bow waiting unitedly to receive me, Slaying, O king, these Kiratas indomitable in battle, by means of these shafts.

verses.sanskrit: सैन्धवस्य वधे यत्तमनुयास्यामि पाण्डवम्।  ये त्वेते सुमहानागा अञ्जनस्य कुलोद्भवाः ॥३३॥
verses.english: I will follow in the track of Pandu's son intent on the slaughter of the Sindhu king. Those other elephants sprung from the race of the Anjanas.

verses.sanskrit: कर्कशाश्च विनीताश्च प्रभिन्नकरटामुखाः।  जाम्बूनदमयैः सर्वैर्वर्मभिः सुविभूषिताः ॥३४॥
verses.english: Of tough hide, well-trained and shedding secretions from their temples and mouth and covered with armours made entirely of gold.
verses.bhavadeepa: अञ्जनस्य अरुणोपवाह्यस्य । ‘स्निग्धनीलाम्बुदप्रख्या बलिनो विपुलैः करैः । सुविभक्तमहाशीर्षाः करिणोञ्जनवंशजाः’ ॥३३॥

verses.sanskrit: लब्धरक्षा रणे राजन्नैरावणसमा युधि।  उत्तरात् पर्वतादेते तीक्ष्णैर्दस्युभिरास्थिताः॥३५॥
verses.english: Those elephants are all very useful in battle and equal to Airavat himself. These have come from the northern hills and are mounted by fierce robbers.

verses.sanskrit: कर्कशैः प्रवरैर्योधैः कार्ष्णायसतनुच्छदैः।  सन्ति गोयोनयश्चात्र सन्ति वानरयोनयः ॥३५॥
verses.english: Those elephants are all very useful in battle and equal to Airavat himself. These have come from the northern hills and are mounted by fierce robbers.

verses.sanskrit: अनेकयोनयश्चान्ये तथा मानुषयोनयः।  अनीकं समवेतानां धूम्रवर्णमुदीर्यते ॥३७॥
verses.english: Possessed of strong limbs, cased in armours and all excellent fighters. There are, amongst them persons born of the cow, of the ape, or of diverse other creatures, including those born of men; that division of the sinful Mlechchas assembled together and come from the strongholds of the Himavat hill, appear to be like volumes of smoke from this distance. Obtaining these and numerous other Kshatriyas.

verses.sanskrit: म्लेच्छानां पापकर्तॄणां हिमदुर्गनिवासिनाम्।  एतद्दुर्योधनो लब्ध्वा समग्रं राजमण्डलम् ॥३८॥
कृपं च सौमदत्तिं च द्रोणं च रथिनां वरम्।  सिन्धुराजं तथा कर्णमवमन्यत पाण्डवान् ॥३९॥
verses.english: As also Kripa and Somadatta's son and that foremost of car-warriors viz., Drona and the ruler of the Sindhus and Karna, as partisans, Duryodhana disregards the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: कृतार्थमथ चात्मानं मन्यते कालचोदितः।  ते तु सर्वेऽद्य संप्राप्ता मम नाराचगोचरम् ॥४०॥
verses.english: He also thinks himself to be already crowned with success, being impelled by Fate. But today, all these warriors, coming within the reach of my Narachas.

verses.sanskrit: न विमोक्ष्यन्ति कौन्तेय यद्यपि स्युर्मनोजवाः।  तेन संभाविता नित्यं परवीर्योपजीविना ॥४१॥
verses.english: Will not escape alive, O son of Kunti, even if they he gifted with the fleetness of the mind. Always held in honour by king Duryodhana ever-depending on the prowess of others.

verses.sanskrit: विनाशमुपयास्यन्ति मच्छरौघनिपीडिताः।  ये त्वेते रथिनो राजन् दृश्यन्ते काञ्चनध्वजाः॥४२॥
verses.english: They shall today meet with their destruction, being sorely afflicted by my arrowy showers. O king, those other warrior owning golden standards, whom you can see.

verses.sanskrit: एते दुर्वारणा नाम काम्बोजा यदि ते श्रुताः।  शूराश्च कृतविद्याश्च धनुर्वेदे च निष्ठिताः ॥४३॥
verses.english: They are known the irresistible Kambojas. They are brave, learned and practised in the use of the bow;

verses.sanskrit: संहताश्च भृशं ह्येते अन्योन्यस्य हितैषिणः।  अक्षौहिण्यश्च संरब्धा धार्तराष्ट्रस्य भारत ॥४४॥
verses.english: They are arranged in serried file and are resolved to stand firmly by one another. These Akshauhini of troops belonging to the sons of Dhritarashtra, all inspired with rage. as are

verses.sanskrit: यत्ता मदर्थे तिष्ठन्ति कुरुवीराभिरक्षिताः।  अप्रमत्ता महाराज मामेव प्रत्युपस्थिताः॥४५॥
verses.english: And expectantly looking for me, awaiting my arrival, being supported by numerous Kuru heroes. They are all coolheaded, O monarch and long to receive me.

verses.sanskrit: तानहं प्रमथिष्यामि तृणानीव हुताशनः।  तस्मात् सर्वानुपासंगान् सर्वोपकरणानि च॥४६॥
verses.english: Them shall I consume, like fire consuming a heap of grass. Let, therefore, o king, those who are versed in equipping chariots, equip my chariot with numerous quivers and all other implements of war and let these weapons be placed in proper places. Weapons of diverse kinds will have to be used in the terrible fight that will commence, ere long.

verses.sanskrit: रथे कुर्वन्तु मे राजन् यथावद्रथकल्पकाः।  अस्मिंस्तु किल संमर्दे ग्राह्यं विविधमायुधम्॥४७॥
यथोपदिष्टमाचार्यैः कार्यः पञ्चगुणो रथः।  काम्बोजैर्हि समेष्यामि तीक्ष्णैराशीविषोपमैः॥४८॥
verses.english: Let the chariot be stuffed with necessaries, five times more then what the professors of military science direct, in as much as, I shall have to encounter the united Kambojas resembling fierce snakes of virulent poison.

verses.sanskrit: नानाशस्त्रसमावायैर्विविधायुधयोधिभिः।  किरातैश्च समेष्यामि विषकल्पैः प्रहारिभिः॥४९॥
verses.english: I shall also have to engage with the Kiratas armed with various implements of war, who resemble virulent poison, who accomplished in striking down.

verses.sanskrit: लालितैः सततं राज्ञा दुर्योधनहितैषिभिः।  शकैश्चापि समेष्यामि शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमैः॥५०॥
verses.english: Who have been favoured by the king and who in consequence, ever desire to achieve the good of Duryodhana. I shall also encounter the Shakas who resemble Indra himself in prowess.

verses.sanskrit: अग्निकल्पैर्दुराधर्षैः प्रदीप्तैरिव पावकैः।  तथान्यैर्विविधैर्योधैः कालकल्पैर्दुरासदैः॥५१॥
verses.english: Who are fierce as fire and difficult of being repressed like a raging conflagration. I shall have also to meet numerous other warriors, all irresistible and resembling Death himself. are

verses.sanskrit: समेष्यामि रणे राजन्बहुभिर्युद्धदुर्मदैः।  तस्माद्वै वाजिनो मुख्या विश्रुताःशुभलक्षणाः॥५२॥
verses.english: I shall have to encounter, O king, countless indomitable warriors. For these reasons, let excellent steeds of the best breed and graced with auspicious marks be harnessed to my chariot, after they had drank their fill and been groomed properly.

verses.sanskrit:
उपावृत्ताश्च पीताश्च पुनर्युज्यन्तु मे रथे।
              सञ्जय उवाच।
              तस्य सर्वानुपासंगान् सर्वोपकरणानि च॥५३॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Then king Yudhishthira directed quivers full of shafts and various other kinds of weapons and all other necessaries, to be placed in the chariot of Satyaki.

verses.sanskrit: रथे चास्थापयद्राजा शस्त्राणि विविधानि च।  ततस्तान् सर्वतो युक्तान् सदश्वांश्चतुरो जनाः॥५४॥
verses.english: Then people caused the four excellent steed yoked to his car to drink juicy and intoxicating liquors.

verses.sanskrit: रसवत्पाययामासुः पानं मदसमीरणम्।  पीतोपवृत्तान्स्नातांश्च जग्धान्नान्समलंकृताम्॥५५॥
verses.english: Having caused those four steeds to slake their thirsts and walk and bathe and eat and having decked them with garlands of gold, men plucked the arrows out of their bodies;

verses.sanskrit: विनीतशल्यांस्तुरगांश्चतुरो हेममालिनः।  तान्युक्तान् रुक्मवर्णाभान् विनीताञ्शीघ्रगामिनः॥५६॥
verses.english: Those animals that had been unharnessed for these operations, that were of golden hue, well-trained, endued with great fleetness, cheerful and extremely docile, were gain properly yoked to his chariot.

verses.sanskrit: संहृष्टमनसोऽव्यग्रान् विधिवत्कल्पितान्रथे।  महाध्वजेन सिंहेन हेमकेसरमालिना ॥५७॥
verses.english: On the top of that chariot was mounted a tall standard bearing the device of a lion of golden manes. The standard was decked with banners of the hue of white clouds and it was graced with golden circles and pearls and corals. An umbrella with a huge golden staff was also placed upon that car that was groaning under the burden of weapons. When those horses decked with golden caparisons had been yoked to the car, the younger brother of Daruka, who was Satyaki's friend and charioteer came and represented to him that the car was ready, even as Matali informs Indra about the equipment of his car.

verses.sanskrit: संवृते केतकैर्हेमैर्मणिविद्रुमचित्रितैः।  पाण्डुराभ्रप्रकाशाभिः पताकाभिरलंकृते॥५८॥
हेमदण्डोच्छ्रितच्छत्रे बहुशस्त्रपरिच्छदे।  योजयामास विधिवद्धेमभाण्डविभूषितान् ॥५९॥
दारुकस्यानुजो भ्राता सूतस्तस्य प्रियः सखा।  न्यवेदयद्रथं युक्तं वासवस्येव मातलिः॥६०॥
ततः स्नातः शुचिर्भूत्वा कृतकौतुकमङ्गलः।  स्नातकानां सहस्रस्य स्वर्णनिष्क्रानथो ददौ॥६१॥
verses.english: Then Satyaki, having taken a bath and having purified himself and having under gone every auspicious ceremony gave away to the Snataka Brahmanas thousand of golden Nikshasas.

verses.sanskrit: आशीर्वादैः परिष्वक्तःसात्यकिः श्रीमतां वरः।  ततः स मधुपर्कार्हः पीत्वा कैलातकं मधु ॥६२॥
verses.english: Then blessed with the benedictions the latter pronounced upon him, that foremost handsome looking men. That hero worthy of adoration, having drunk Kailataka honey, appeared exceedingly beautiful with reddened eyes rolling in intoxication. Having touched a brazen mirror and being highly delighted, he became filled the double his ordinary energy and looked like the blazing fire.

verses.sanskrit: लोहिताक्षो बभौ तत्र मद‌विह्वललोचनः।  आलभ्य वीरकांस्यं च हर्षेण महताऽन्वितः॥६३॥
द्विगुणीकृततेजा हि प्रज्वलन्निव पावकः।  उत्सङ्गे धनुरादाय सशरं रथिनां वरः ॥६४॥
verses.english: Taking upon his shoulder his bow and arrows that best of car-warriors, covered in mail and adorned with ornaments, made the twice-born perform the rites of propitiation on his behalf. ones

verses.sanskrit: कृतस्वस्त्ययनो विप्रैः कवची समलंकृतः।  लाजैर्गन्धैस्तथा माल्यैः कन्याभिश्चाभिनन्दितः॥६५॥
verses.english: Handsome damsels then adored him by covering him with a shower of fried paddy, perfumes and garlands of flowers. Thereafter that brave warrior with folded palms worshipped Yudhishthira's feet; whereupon the latter smelt his head. Having undergone all these ceremonies he mounted his chariot. Thereafter those horses, cheerful, plump, of the fleetness of the wind. Invincible in battle and of the Sindhu breed, were on the point of dragging that excellent chariot of Satyaki. Bhimasena also similarly, honoured by the very virtuous king Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: युधिष्ठिरस्य चरणावभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः।  तेन मूर्धन्युपाघ्रात आरुरोह महारथम् ॥६६॥
ततस्ते वाजिनो हृष्टाः सुपुष्ठा वातरंहसः।  अजय्या जैत्रमूहुस्तं विकुर्वाणाः स्म सैन्धवाः॥६७॥
तथैव भीमसेनोऽपि धर्मराजेन पूजितः।  प्रायात्सात्यकिना सार्थमभिवाद्य युविाष्ठरम्॥६८॥
verses.english: Set out with Satyaki, after having duly saluted the king (Yudhishthira). Beholding these two scorchers of foes cast their glances on your army.

verses.sanskrit: तौ दृष्ट्वा प्रविविक्षन्तौ तव सेनामरिन्द‌मौ।  संयत्तास्तावकाः सर्वे तस्थुर्द्रोणपुरोगमाः ॥६९॥
सन्नद्धमनुगच्छन्तं दृष्ट्वा भीमं स सात्यकिः।  अभिनन्द्याब्रवीद्वीरस्तदा हर्षकरं वचः॥७०॥
त्वं भीम रक्ष राजानमेतत्कार्यतमं हि ते।  अहं भित्त्वा प्रवेक्ष्यामि कालपक्वमिदं बलम्॥७१॥
आयत्यां च तदात्वे च श्रेयो राज्ञोऽभिरक्षणम्।  जानीषे मम वीर्यं त्वं तव चाहमरिन्दम ॥७२॥
तस्माद्भीम निवर्तस्व मम चेदिच्छसि प्रियम्। तथोक्तः सात्यकिं प्राह व्रज त्वं कार्यसिद्धये॥७३॥
verses.english: Therefore, O Bhima, turn back, if you, desire to do my good.” Thus spoken to Bhima replied to Satyaki saying “Go you then and be victorious and successful!

verses.sanskrit: अहं राज्ञः करिष्यामि रक्षां पुरुषसत्तम।  एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच भीमसेनं स माधवः॥७४॥
verses.english: O foremost of men, I will protect the king to the best of my prowess." "Being thus addressed he of Madhu's race, replied to Bhimasena sayingगच्छ गच्छ ध्रुवं पार्थ ध्रुवो हि विजयो मम।

verses.sanskrit: गच्छ गच्छ ध्रुवं पार्थ ध्रुवो हि विजयो मम।  यन्मे गुणानुरक्तश्च त्वमद्य वशमास्थितः ॥७५॥
verses.english: "Turn back, turn back, O son of Pritha; my victory today is certain in as much as you, won over by my merits, are now intent to carry out my wishes.

verses.sanskrit: निमित्तानि च धन्यानि यथा भीम वदन्ति माम्।  निहते सैन्धवे पापे पाण्डवेन महात्मना ॥७६॥
verses.english: These auspicious omens also indicate my victory. When the sinful ruler of the Sindhus will be slain by the high-souled son of Pandu (Arjuna).

verses.sanskrit: परिष्वजिष्ये राजानं धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्।  एतावदुक्त्वा भीमं तु विसृज्य च महायशाः॥७७॥
verses.english: I shall embrace the illustrious king viz., Yudhishthira.” Having thus spoken to Bhima, the high-famed Satyaki left him. He then cast his eyes on your troops like a tiger looking at herds of deer.

verses.sanskrit: संप्रैक्षत्तावकं सैन्यं व्याघ्रो मृगगणानिव॥७८॥
तं दृष्ट्वा प्रविविक्षन्तं सैन्यं तव जनाधिप।  भूय एवाभवन्मूढं सुभृशं चाप्यकम्पत ॥७९॥
ततः प्रयातः सहसा तव सैन्यं स सात्याकः।  दिदृक्षुरर्जुनं राजन् धर्मराजस्य शासनात्॥८०॥
